candidate.answerReason: The right angle at A is divided in the ratio 1:3, giving angles of 22.5 and 67.5 degrees. Right-triangle complements and equal half-diagonals then give \(\angle DAC=22.5^\circ\), so \(\angle EAC=45^\circ\).

methods.label: Use equal half-diagonals
methods.explanation: \(\angle BAE=22.5^\circ\) and \(\angle DAE=67.5^\circ\). In right triangle \(ABE\), \(\angle ABD=67.5^\circ\), so \(\angle ADB=22.5^\circ\). Since \(OA=OD\), \(\angle DAO=22.5^\circ\). Therefore, \(\angle EAC=67.5^\circ-22.5^\circ=45^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses Grade 8 rectangle and isosceles-triangle properties with elementary angle calculations.

methods.label: Use congruent triangles
methods.explanation:
The perpendicular \(AE\) splits the right angle \(DAB\) into angles in the ratio \(1:3\), so \(\angle BAE=90^\circ/4=22.5^\circ\). In right triangle \(ABE\), this gives \(\angle ABD=90^\circ-22.5^\circ=67.5^\circ\).

To find the angle made by \(AC\), compare \(\triangle BAD\) and \(\triangle ABC\). They have \(BA=AB\), \(AD=BC\), and \(\angle BAD=\angle ABC=90^\circ\), so they are congruent by SAS. Corresponding angles give \(\angle BAC=\angle ABD=67.5^\circ\). Both \(AE\) and \(AC\) lie inside the right angle at \(A\), so
\[
\angle EAC=\angle BAC-\angle BAE
=67.5^\circ-22.5^\circ=45^\circ.
\]
methods.levelReason: SAS congruence and corresponding-angle equality are Grade 8 topics. This route transfers an angle through congruence instead of using equal half-diagonals.

review.mathematicalCheck: The altitude from the right-angle vertex of triangle ABD meets segment BD, so AE splits angle DAB. The ratio gives \(\angle BAE=22.5^\circ\), then \(\angle ABD=67.5^\circ\) and \(\angle ADB=22.5^\circ\). Equal half-diagonals give \(\angle DAO=22.5^\circ\), hence \(\angle EAC=45^\circ\). Independently, the stated SAS correspondence between BAD and ABC correctly gives \(\angle BAC=67.5^\circ\), yielding the same difference. Both explanations are sufficient.
